designDecisionsAndRationale: Section 17.13 classifies the historical failures as date consumer, live inactivity, executable discovery, sandbox, CLI diagnostic, callable metadata, usage/add-on investigation, admission and add-on availability boundaries.
Two independent first-wave plans cover CLI fixtures and Work/Core fixtures; one dependent serial plan joins evidence, reconciles edits and verifies the combined tree.
Specific diagnostics, positive and negative controls and side-effect assertions prevent fixture repairs from hiding production failures.
intentionalTradeoffs: The exact usage/add-on failure cause remains an implementation investigation until its diagnostic is captured.
Historical aggregate failures remain failed evidence until replaced by current-source exit-zero logs; implementation, independent reviews and publication are pending.
supportedEdgeCases: Scratch-path executable discovery must launch the current built CLI in a separate process with an isolated home.
Stale inactivity observations must reject without changing task/attempt decisions; admission rejection must be distinguished from preflight validation and adapter execution.
Unresolved add-ons must retain a negative diagnostic while successful temporary registration uses a resolvable add-on.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: No workflow package, prompt, skill or package digest change is planned.
No browser or UI verification is required for these source/test edits.
